newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends firmer but off highs.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends firmer but off highs.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer but off its highs on Monday, retaining a bid tone on the back of the Australian dollar.
The Kiwi finished at US$0.6969/76 and 68.77 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.6950/57 and 68.61 at the open.
Dealers said one local bank showed a strong appetite for the currency around the mid-session, pushing it briefly to a high of 0.6983 amid some talk of possible Euro and samurai-related interest.
The Kiwi then backed off slightly after running into corporate selling at 0.6980.
"Underlyingly, it still remains bid on the back of the Aussie," a dealer said, adding he expected a push up towards 70 U.S. cents overnight.

Dealers were sceptical whether Tuesday's Quarterly Employment Survey would provoke much more than an initial scurry in the currency, though the data is seen as important for the Reserve Bank as it prepares its March 13 economic forecasts and decides whether to seek an early tightening in monetary conditions.
Economists predict a rise in total ordinary time wages of around 0.7 percent for the quarter and 3.5 percent for the year.
